title: 01. Foundations: How LLMs Actually Work
summary: An LLM (Large Language Model) is a next-token predictor. That's it.

sections.title: Plain English First
sections.body:
An LLM (Large Language Model) is a **next-token predictor**. That's it. It reads everything you give it and predicts what word/token should come next — one token at a time.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              HOW AN LLM GENERATES TEXT                          │
│                                                                 │
│  YOU GIVE IT:                                                   │
│  "The capital of France is"                                     │
│            │                                                    │
│            ▼                                                    │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                  LLM ENGINE                             │   │
│  │                                                         │   │
│  │  Step 1: TOKENIZE                                       │   │
│  │  "The" "capital" "of" "France" "is"                     │   │
│  │    ↓       ↓      ↓     ↓       ↓                       │   │
│  │  [464]  [3361]  [286] [4881]  [318]                     │   │
│  │                                                         │   │
│  │  Step 2: EMBED (convert to vectors)                     │   │
│  │  Each token → list of 12,288 numbers                    │   │
│  │  "France" → [0.2, -0.8, 0.3, 0.7, ...]                 │   │
│  │                                                         │   │
│  │  Step 3: SELF-ATTENTION                                 │   │
│  │  Every token looks at every other token                 │   │
│  │  "is" pays attention to "capital" and "France"          │   │
│  │  Because they are semantically linked                   │   │
│  │                                                         │   │
│  │  Step 4: PREDICT NEXT TOKEN                             │   │
│  │  "Paris"    → probability: 0.92 ← WINNER               │   │
│  │  "Lyon"     → probability: 0.04                         │   │
│  │  "Berlin"   → probability: 0.02                         │   │
│  │  "London"   → probability: 0.01                         │   │
│  │  others...  → probability: 0.01                         │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│            │                                                    │
│            ▼                                                    │
│  IT OUTPUTS:  "Paris"                                           │
│                                                                 │
│  Then it loops: "The capital of France is Paris"                │
│  → predicts next token → " ."  → stops                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Why This Matters for Agents
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│          WHY LLM MECHANICS MATTER FOR AGENT BUILDERS            │
│                                                                 │
│  ❶ LLMs have NO MEMORY between calls                           │
│     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────      │
│     Each API call is completely fresh.                          │
│     Solution: YOU must inject history into every prompt.        │
│                                                                 │
│     Call 1: "What is Python?"  → "Python is..."                │
│     Call 2: "Tell me more"     → LLM has NO idea about Call 1  │
│             Unless you include Call 1 in the prompt!            │
│                                                                 │
│  ❷ LLMs are PROBABILISTIC — not deterministic                  │
│     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────      │
│     Same input can give different outputs (unless temp=0)       │
│     For agents: USE temperature=0 for tool calls & reasoning    │
│                 USE temperature>0 for creative generation        │
│                                                                 │
│  ❸ LLMs HALLUCINATE when they don't know                       │
│     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────      │
│     They always predict a token — even if that token is wrong   │
│     "What is veerababu74dd's phone number?" → makes one up!     │
│     Solution: RAG + Tool use + Faithfulness checks              │
│                                                                 │
│  ❹ CONTEXT WINDOW is a hard limit                              │
│     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────      │
│     GPT-4o: 128,000 tokens maximum                              │
│     Everything — system prompt, history, tools, docs —          │
│     must fit inside this window. Nothing else exists for LLM.  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
